theme: 旅游 · 餐厅点餐与小费文化
goals: 掌握餐厅预约、点餐及结账的核心句型
理解美国小费文化的计算方式与社交规则
熟悉菜单常见分类与食物烹饪程度表达
积累 30 个餐饮场景高频词汇与地道搭配

tasks.text: 精读前 5 篇短文，标注生词并朗读
观看前 3 个视频，模仿点餐对话语音语调
精读后 5 篇短文，总结小费计算规则
观看后 3 个视频，完成情景模拟练习

mustLearn.title: 点餐核心句型
mustLearn.content: I'd like to order... / Could I have...? / How would you like your steak? 中文讲解：点餐时常用 I'd like 比 I want 更礼貌。询问牛排熟度用 How would you like... 要点解析：注意 would like 后接名词或 to do， steak 熟度分为 rare, medium, well-done。

mustLearn.title: 小费表达法
mustLearn.content: Is tip included? / I'll leave a 20% tip. 中文讲解：询问账单是否含服务费，或主动说明小费比例。要点解析：include 表示包含，leave a tip 是固定搭配，表示留下小费。

mustLearn.title: 结账请求
mustLearn.content: Could we get the check, please? / Can I pay by card? 中文讲解：美式英语用 check 表示账单，英式用 bill。要点解析：pay by card 或 pay with cash，介词搭配需记忆。

mustLearn.title: 饮食禁忌表达
mustLearn.content: I am allergic to... / Does this contain...? 中文讲解：表达过敏用 be allergic to，询问成分用 contain。要点解析：allergy 是名词，allergic 是形容词，注意词性变化。

expand.title: 小费比例参考
expand.content: 美国餐厅午餐通常 15%-18%，晚餐 18%-20%。服务极佳可给 25%，服务差可给 10% 但需说明原因。

expand.title: 菜单术语辨析
expand.content: Appetizer 是开胃菜，Entree 在主菜前（美式）或即主菜（英式），Side dish 是配菜。

expand.title: 支付常用语
expand.content: Split the bill 表示 AA 制分开付账，Cover 表示请客买单，如 I'll cover this one.

expand.title: 牛排熟度英文
expand.content: Rare 一分熟，Medium Rare 三分熟，Medium 五分熟，Well-done 全熟。中国游客常选 Medium 或 Well-done。

expand.title: 礼貌用语升级
expand.content: 将 I want 替换为 I'd like 或 Could I have，将 Give me 替换为 Can I get，语气更柔和。

articles.title: Booking a Table
articles.content: When you travel to a new city, popular restaurants are often busy. It is smart to make a reservation before you go. You can call the restaurant or use an app like OpenTable. When you call, tell them how many people are in your group and what time you want to eat. For example, say, 'I'd like to book a table for four at 7 PM.' They might ask for your name and phone number. If you arrive late, they might give your table to someone else. So, always try to be on time. Some places also have a waiting list if you walk in without a booking.
articles.zh: 介绍旅行时如何预约餐厅座位及注意事项。
points: make a reservation 表示预约座位
book a table for... 后接人数

articles.title: Understanding the Menu
articles.content: When you sit down, the waiter will give you a menu. Menus usually have different sections. First, you see Appetizers or Starters. These are small dishes to eat before the main meal. Then there are Salads and Soups. The main part is called Entrees or Main Courses. Here you find meat, fish, or pasta. Finally, there is Dessert for something sweet after eating. Drinks are often on a separate list. If you do not understand a word, just ask the waiter. They can explain what is in the dish. It is okay to ask questions before you order.
articles.zh: 讲解菜单的基本结构与各部分名称。
points: separate list 表示单独的清单

articles.title: Starting with Drinks
articles.content: Usually, the first thing you order is drinks. The waiter might ask, 'Would you like something to drink?' You can order water, soda, juice, or wine. Tap water is often free in American restaurants. If you want ice, say 'with ice.' If you prefer no ice, say 'no ice, please.' For alcohol, you need to show your ID if you look young. Beer and wine are common choices. Coffee or tea usually comes after the meal, but you can order them anytime. Don't forget to check if refills are free. Some places charge for extra cups of coffee.
articles.zh: 描述点饮料的流程与常见选项。
points: Tap water 指自来水（免费）
show your ID 出示身份证件

articles.title: Choosing Appetizers
articles.content: Appetizers are great for sharing with friends. Common options include nachos, wings, or calamari. If you are hungry, you can order more than one. If you are on a diet, you might choose a small salad. You can ask the waiter for recommendations. They know what is popular today. Sometimes there are daily specials that are not on the regular menu. These specials might be cheaper or tastier. Just ask, 'What do you recommend?' or 'What is the special today?' It helps you try something new and delicious without taking too much risk.
articles.zh: 介绍开胃菜的选择与询问推荐的方式。
points: sharing with friends 与朋友分享

articles.title: Main Course Choices
articles.content: Choosing the main course is the most important part. You might see steak, chicken, fish, or vegetarian options. If you eat meat, think about how you want it cooked. For chicken, it is usually fully cooked. For fish, it depends on the type. Vegetarian dishes use vegetables instead of meat. Vegans do not eat any animal products. If you are unsure, ask about the ingredients. Some sauces have cream or butter. If you are healthy-conscious, ask for sauce on the side. This way, you can control how much you eat. Enjoy your favorite flavor.
articles.zh: 讲解主菜选择及烹饪方式与饮食偏好。
points: sauce on the side 酱汁分开放

articles.title: Cooking Preferences
articles.content: When you order steak, the waiter will ask about doneness. Rare means red inside. Medium means pink inside. Well-done means fully cooked with no pink. Most people prefer Medium or Medium Rare. If you like it very soft, choose Rare. If you like it hard, choose Well-done. For eggs, you can say scrambled, fried, or boiled. Scramled eggs are mixed and cooked in a pan. Fried eggs have a yellow yolk in the center. Boiled eggs are cooked in water. Tell the waiter clearly so you get what you like. Nobody wants to eat cold or wrong food.
articles.zh: 说明肉类熟度与鸡蛋做法的英文表达。

articles.title: During the Meal
articles.content: While you are eating, the waiter might check on you. They will ask, 'Is everything okay?' If you need more water or napkins, just raise your hand. Do not shout. A simple smile and eye contact work well. If something is wrong, tell them politely. For example, if the food is cold, say, 'Excuse me, this is a bit cold.' They will usually fix it or bring a new one. Remember, they are there to help you. Being rude does not help anyone. A kind word makes the service better for everyone at the table.
articles.zh: 描述用餐过程中与服务员的互动礼仪。
points: check on you 查看你的情况
raise your hand 举手示意

articles.title: Asking for the Bill
articles.content: When you finish eating, you need to pay. In America, you ask for the 'check.' In other countries, people say 'bill.' You can say, 'Could we get the check, please?' The waiter will bring a small folder with the paper inside. Check the numbers to make sure they are correct. Sometimes there are mistakes. If you split the bill, tell them early. Some restaurants allow splitting by item. Others just split the total equally. If you pay together, one person pays and others give cash later. Decide this before the waiter comes back.
articles.zh: 讲解结账时的用语与分单方式。
points: ask for the check 索要账单
split the bill 分开付账

articles.title: How to Tip
articles.content: Tipping is very important in the US. Waiters earn low wages and depend on tips. The standard is 15% to 20% of the total bill. If the service is good, give 20%. If it is okay, give 15%. You calculate this based on the amount before tax. Some receipts have lines for tip and total. Write the tip amount and add it to the bill. Then sign your name. If you pay by card, you can add the tip on the machine. Cash tips are also welcome. Never leave zero tip unless the service was terrible.
articles.zh: 说明美国小费的标准与计算方法。
points: depend on tips 依赖小费

articles.title: Tipping Etiquette
articles.content: Different services have different tipping rules. For sit-down restaurants, 15-20% is normal. For fast food, you do not need to tip. For coffee shops, one dollar or some coins are nice. If someone carries your bags at a hotel, give one or two dollars per bag. Taxi drivers also expect 10-15%. Tour guides should get a tip too. It shows you appreciate their work. If you are unsure, look at what others do. Or just ask a local friend. Being generous makes your trip smoother and people happier.
articles.zh: 介绍不同服务场景下的小费礼仪。
points: appreciate their work 感谢他们的工作
